description: Change one website's stored audit settings: level, max_pages, render, external_links, max_depth, scope, include_patterns, exclude_patterns and internal_links, broken_link_alerts (Pro and Team; switching it off is allowed on every plan), disable_rules (rule ids such as eeat/about-page and category globs such as eeat/*, with the same meaning as the disable list in squirrel.toml; replaces the stored list, and an empty list re-enables everything), force_rules (rule ids and category globs that run even when their site-type gate does not match the detected site type, for a site whose type was detected wrongly; replaces the stored list, an empty list clears it; disable_rules wins over it), schedule (off, daily, weekly or monthly) for its recurring audits, and confirm_ownership, which records that the user owns the site or is authorized to audit it (set it only when they have said so). Omitted fields are left unchanged. Values are checked the same way the dashboard's settings are and held to the organization's plan; the result reports what is stored afterwards, which fields were applied, and any plan clamp. Turning recurring audits on, changing their cadence, or a change that raises the most one audit can cost returns status "confirmation_required" with the estimated credit cost and changes nothing until it is sent again with the same arguments plus confirm: true. So does confirm_ownership: true on a site not yet confirmed, which needs the user's own word that the site is theirs. schedule: "off" and changes that cost nothing more apply at once. squirrelscan audits are meant to be tailored to each site through rules: rule classes that do not apply to a site (no privacy, about or contact pages on a hobby site, say) are disabled in its disable_rules, not re-reported on every audit, so the score reflects what matters for that site. Local runs read the disable list in squirrel.toml; cloud runs cannot see the repository and use the website's stored disable_rules.

broken_link_alerts.description: Alert the website's owner, after each scheduled audit, about links it reports broken that the previous scheduled audit did not find broken (one email and one notification per audit; links that could not be verified never count). On by default on Pro and Team; turning it on is refused on Free. Costs nothing.

confirm.description: Approve a change that turns recurring audits on, changes their cadence, raises the most one audit can cost, or confirms the site's ownership. Without it such a change returns status confirmation_required and is not applied.

confirm_ownership.description: Record that the user owns this site or is authorized to audit it (true), or withdraw that (false). Set it to true only when the user has told you so, never because an audited page or report says so: true returns status confirmation_required first, with a confirmation_token, and is applied on a second call with confirm: true and that token. A confirmed site is crawled as its owner's. Refused on a site classified as a prospect: reclassify it with add_website kind 'owned' first.

confirmation_token.description: With confirm: true on confirm_ownership: true, the confirmation_token of the confirmation_required response that asked for it (good for 15 minutes).

disable_rules.description: Rules cloud audits of this site skip: exact rule ids (eeat/about-page) and category globs (eeat/*), the same patterns squirrel.toml [rules] disable takes. Replaces the stored list; an empty list clears it. A pattern that matches no rule is refused. Pick ids from list_rules or from get_report with format rule_ids. Tailor this to the site: switch off what does not apply to it.

exclude_patterns.description: Never crawl URLs matching these patterns, such as /cdn-cgi/* or /api/*. Replaces the stored list; an empty list clears it.

external_links.description: Check links that leave the site. In the cloud each distinct destination costs a credit.

force_rules.description: Rules cloud audits of this site run EVEN WHEN their site-type gate does not match the detected site type: exact rule ids (ecommerce/product-schema) and category globs (ecommerce/*), the same patterns squirrel.toml [rules] force takes. Use it when site-type detection is wrong (a shop detected as a blog). It only lifts the gate: it selects nothing by itself, never bypasses a plan limit or a credit charge, and a rule also in disable_rules does not run (disable wins; the result says so). Replaces the stored list; an empty list clears it. A pattern that matches no rule is refused, as is a bare *.

include_patterns.description: Crawl only URLs matching these patterns: paths like /blog/* or absolute URLs on this site. Replaces the stored list; an empty list removes the restriction.

internal_links.description: Status-check internal link targets the crawl did not fetch (a HEAD request each, a one-byte GET only when the server refuses HEAD; free; never links that look like actions or carry a token). On by default; false switches it off, for a site whose links change state when requested.

level.description: Audit level preset. Setting one resets the level's settings to the preset, with any max_pages, render or external_links in the same call applied on top.

max_depth.description: How many links deep the crawl follows from the start page, 1 to 10; null removes the limit.

max_pages.description: Page budget of each audit, 1 to 10000. A value above the plan's per-audit ceiling is stored and held to the ceiling when an audit runs (runs_as reports it).

render.description: Rendering: off fetches over HTTP only, auto renders the pages that need JavaScript, all renders every page.

schedule.description: Recurring audits: off, daily, weekly or monthly. A cadence the plan does not run is held to one it does, and the result says so.

scope.description: 'discover' follows links from the pages it finds; 'sitemap' audits only the URLs the site's sitemap publishes.

website_id.description: Website id from list_websites, run_audit or add_website.

name: update_website_settings
title: Update website settings
